newsitem.title: USA: Anvil Range says still no sign of restart.
newsitem.headline: Anvil Range says still no sign of restart.

text.p: Anvil Range Mining Corp said there was still no decision regarding when mining would restart as the production of concentrates comes to an end.
Anvil suspended mining on December 20 because of lower than expected base metal prices, a strong Canadian dollar and dealys in stripping the mine.

On Wednesday Anvil said milling operations would cease on March 31. More money and better metal prices were needed before its Faro operation, one of the world's biggest zinc and lead mines, was restarted.
"Before operations can restart, the company will need to commence a stripping programme which is expected to take approximately three months to complete," the company said.
The closure of Faro helped to set the scene for more favourable terms for miners in selling their lead and zinc concentrates to smelters in 1997 contracts.
Although Cominco injected $9.4 million into the company by raising its stake to 28 percent, more cash is needed.
On Wednesday Anvil said it had restated its results after changing its year end to December 31 from October 31.
In the 14 months ended December 31, 1996 Anvil's revenues totalled $214.1 million from the production of 345,700 tonnes of zinc concentrates and 186,000 tonnes of lead concentrates.
For the same period Anvil reported a net loss of $35.3 million or $2.15 per common share.
In the period realised prices for zinc and lead were 46 U.S. cents and 34 U.S. cents per pound, respectively.
Since December the Canadian dollar has weakened against the U.S. dollar, the currency base metals are traded in. In addition zinc prices have risen sharply.
Cash LME zinc on Wednesday settled at 56 cents a pound after hitting a four-and-a-half-year high on Monday.
